messages:
Maria K.: FYI we're seeing exporter gRPC streams stall intermittently from Dedicated pools. Spans queue up for ~30s and then exporter reports 'send failed' and we see dropped spans in metrics. Noticed after the quota change yesterday.
Ajay (aj): Hmm. Is this the OTLP collector or our in-process exporter? Which path? @Maria K. can you paste the logs?
Maria K.: in-process exporter (redwood-infer runtime). Logs: `exporter: send failed: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = transport is closing` repeated, then `exporter buffer overflow, dropping 12 spans`.
Lee: Likely a gRPC stream stall + no fallback to http in that codepath. We've previously assumed gRPC forever for latency but that's brittle under transient conn stalls. Two quick angles: 1) tune timeouts/backoff, 2) implement fast http fallback for short-lived stalls.
Priya: Also the quota change reduced per-tenant egress tokens which means bursts get queued longer. We should correlate tenant id -> queue depth before flipping fallback — don't want cross-tenant noisiness.
Ajay (aj): Agreed. Proposed config snippet for runtime (untested):
```
exporter:
  otlp:
    protocol: grpc
    grpc:
      send_timeout_ms: 10000
      max_retries: 5
      backoff_ms: 200
      max_backoff_ms: 5000
    http_fallback:
      enabled: true
      activation_queue_ms: 2000
    queue:
      max_size: 20000
      per_tenant_max: 5000
```
Sam: A couple notes: 1) set backoff with jitter, 2) we should gate http fallback with an idempotency header to avoid duplicate spans being ingested as unique — OTLP doesn't dedupe. Can we add a span-batch-id header? 3) health probe on exporter stream so the router can route to a different region temporarily.
Maria K.: Good call on jitter. We currently include a batch UUID in metadata for debugging but not for dedupe. Dedupe at ingestion is expensive.
Lee: Instead of dedupe, keep fallback window tiny (2s) + hedging: if gRPC doesn't ack within X ms, fire an http call for the same batch but mark it as 'maybe-duplicate' in metadata so downstream can be lax. Also circuit-breaker: after N failures for tenant, apply stricter batching/limits.
Priya: I'll map tenant quotas -> retention/queue limits to ensure we don't OOM. Also we should surface per-tenant queue depth to console dashboards and alert when >75% of per_tenant_max.
infra-bot: alert: exporter_queue_depth{tenant="redwood-prod-1"} = 4200 (threshold 3750)
Ajay (aj): Action items: (1) Spike a PR with send_timeout + jittered backoff + http_fallback flag (2) Add per-tenant queue metric to telemetry and dashboard (3) Small runbook for oncall to flip fallback false/true. I'll open tickets.
Sam: I'll take the PR for the fallback hedging logic and write a microbenchmark for duplicate rate.
Maria K.: Thanks — also can we add a short-term mitigation: increase per_tenant_max to 8k while we iterate? Need to file infra cost approval but prevents immediate drops.
Priya: on it, will queue the change with cost note. tagging @eng-oncall for visibility. :eyes:
Maria K.: Nice. If anyone sees the pattern again, post logs and span-batch-id. :thumbsup:
